stem.text: The diagram shows naturally occurring D-glucose and a form of glucose that can be synthesised in the laboratory, known as L-glucose.

stem.alt: Ring structure drawing of a glucose molecule labelled D-glucose
stem.label: D-glucose

stem.alt: Ring structure drawing of a glucose molecule labelled L-glucose
stem.label: L-glucose

stem.text: The enzyme glucose oxidase catalyses the oxidation of D-glucose. The enzyme **cannot** catalyse the oxidation of L-glucose.
Which statement about L-glucose explains this?

A.text: L-glucose does **not** fit into the active site of glucose oxidase.

B.text: L-glucose has a different structural formula to D-glucose.

D.text: L-glucose is the mirror image of D-glucose.
